title: Plan AU: AI Fitness & Health Plan
summary: Assessment → training plan → nutrition → check-ins → periodization
scenario: For fitness beginners customizing training and nutrition around their own situation; not medical advice — see a doctor first if you have injuries or chronic conditions.

steps.title: Assess baseline
steps.detail: Record height, weight, body fat if known, age, sex, schedule, injury history, current activity level and goal (fat loss / muscle gain / recomp / fitness). Have the model set a baseline of what you can do now — don't start at high intensity.
steps.tips: List any sore or injured body part explicitly and have the model avoid related movements — this isn't a minor detail.

steps.title: Training plan
steps.detail: Have the model lay out a plan across your available days (aim for 3-4): how strength / cardio / rest days distribute, and each exercise's sets, reps and rest. Ask for form cues and common mistakes, plus why this arrangement.
steps.tips: Ask for a table — 'exercise | sets × reps | weight cue | form points' — so you can follow it at the gym.

steps.title: Nutrition
steps.detail: Based on your goal (deficit for fat loss, surplus for muscle gain), have the model estimate daily protein/carb/fat ratios and rough calories, with swap-in food examples. Skip precise counting — palm/fist estimates are more sustainable.
steps.tips: Change just one thing first (like swapping the sugary drink at dinner), not every habit at once.

steps.title: Check-ins
steps.detail: After each workout, log exercises and weights in Keep, or use a Notion check-in page for completion, feel (easy/hard/impossible), sleep and weight trend. Records are the basis for adjustment.
steps.tips: Log only two fields — 'done or not' and 'how it felt' — five seconds keeps the habit alive.

steps.title: Periodization
steps.detail: Feed the last 2-4 weeks of check-ins to the model to review progress: did weights go up, did body weight or measurements change, how do you feel — then adjust weight, exercises or frequency (progressive overload). At a plateau, swap exercises or add volume.
steps.tips: Have the model compare last week's completed weights to this week's for concrete numbers — don't just stare at the scale.

pitfalls.title: Treating the AI plan as medical advice
pitfalls.detail: AI doesn't know your history or body; stop any movement that causes discomfort, and consult a doctor or certified coach for pre-existing conditions.

pitfalls.title: Starting way too intense
pitfalls.detail: Beginners who hit high intensity in week one are injured or quit by week two; make 'showing up consistently' the goal for the first two weeks.

pitfalls.title: Planning without executing
pitfalls.detail: A plan in your saved folder burns zero calories; check-ins plus a weekly review are the engine — run four weeks and look at data.

pitfalls.title: Ignoring recovery and sleep
pitfalls.detail: Gains happen in recovery; training hard without sleep stalls progress anyway — schedule sleep and rest days into the plan.
